message.content:
Using  
\[
\sin A=\cos B \iff \sin A=\sin\left(\frac\pi2-B\right),
\]
we have
\[
\sin(\pi\cos x)=\cos(\pi\sin x)
\]
so
\[
\sin(\pi\cos x)=\sin\left(\frac\pi2-\pi\sin x\right).
\]

Thus either
\[
\pi\cos x=\frac\pi2-\pi\sin x+2k\pi
\]
or
\[
\pi\cos x=\pi-\left(\frac\pi2-\pi\sin x\right)+2k\pi.
\]

Dividing by \(\pi\):

1. \(\cos x=\frac12-\sin x+2k\), so
\[
\sin x+\cos x=\frac12+2k.
\]
Since \(|\sin x+\cos x|\le \sqrt2\), only \(k=0\) works, giving
\[
\sin x+\cos x=\frac12.
\]
Squaring:
\[
1+\sin 2x=\frac14 \implies \sin 2x=-\frac34.
\]

2. \(\cos x=\frac12+\sin x+2k\), so
\[
\cos x-\sin x=\frac12+2k.
\]
Again only \(k=0\) works, giving
\[
\cos x-\sin x=\frac12.
\]
Squaring:
\[
1-\sin 2x=\frac14 \implies \sin 2x=\frac34.
\]

Therefore the possible values are
\[
\boxed{-\frac34,\frac34}.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{-\frac34,\frac34}\).
